# Ziziphora clinopodioides Lam.

First published in Tabl. Encycl. 1: 63 (1791)

This species is accepted

The native range of this species is Temp. Asia. It is a subshrub and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

## Descriptions

### According to Flora of Iraq

Ghazanfar, S., Edmondson, J., & Haloob, A. (Eds.). (2026). Flora of Iraq Volume 7: Solanaceae to Biebersteiniaceae. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.

Morphology General Habit
    Suffruticose, often mat-forming perennial
Morphology Stem
    Stems prostrate to erect, usually much branched from base, 5–50 cm tall, glabrous to hirsute, sometimes pilose above
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves very variable in size and shape, 4–15 × 2–6 mm, linear-lanceolate to ovate-oblong, rarely suborbicular to orbicular, petiolate to 2.5 mm long, attenuate, cuneate or rounded at base, acute to acuminate at apex, entire or slightly serrulate, glabrous to ± pilose or velutinous with sessile glands
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences

Ghazanfar, S., Edmondson, J., & Haloob, A. (Eds.). (2026). Flora of Iraq Volume 7: Solanaceae to Biebersteiniaceae. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.

Morphology Stem
    Flowering stems to 10 cm tall, arcuate-ascending, green to purplish, pubescent
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves broadly ovate to elliptic, or orbicular, rounded at base, often acuminate-apiculate at apex, sparsely papillose-puberulent to glabrescent, veins prominent beneath
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Calyx
    Calyx 5–6 mm long, sparsely to densely hirsute-villous, whitish-green.
Ecology
    Rocky slopes and screes, mixed shrubland on mountain
Altitude
    alt. 1500–3400 m;
Phenology
    flowering & fruiting Jul.-Sep
Distribution
    Rare in the upper forest and lower thorn-cushion zones, and in the lower forest zone of Iraq. E. Turkey, N.W. Iran.
